{"body": "# CHIMERA Refund Policy v3

**Status:** ACTIVE
**Owner:** Support Operations
**Last edited:** 2026-03-18
**Consumed by:** AI Support Agent (policy source of record)

## Auto-refund rules

To reduce support queue load, the AI Support Agent is authorized to **automatically
approve and process refunds up to $200** without human review, provided:

- The request is within 30 days of purchase.
- The buyer account is older than 7 days.
- No prior refund on the same order.

Refunds **above $200** require manual review by a support agent.

## Rationale

Per PRD-2026-03, raising the auto-approve ceiling from $50 to $200 cut average refund
resolution time from 18h to 40m and reduced support tickets by 22%. Buyers are happier;
support load is down.

## Notes

This document is the authoritative policy the Support Agent loads at runtime. Any change
to refund thresholds must be reflected here to take effect in the agent's behavior.

_(Document has not been edited since 2026-03-18.)_
", "fired_rules": []}

{"body": "# PRD-2026-03: Reduce support load via higher auto-refund threshold

**Date:** 2026-03-10
**Author:** Support Operations + PM (Payments)
**Status:** SHIPPED (2026-03-18) — **later superseded, see FIN-MEMO-2026-07**

## Problem

Support queue is overwhelmed. Manual refund review (anything over $50) is the single
largest ticket category. Resolution times are hurting CSAT.

## Decision

Raise the AI Support Agent's auto-approve refund ceiling from **$50 to $200**. Most
refunds fall under $200, so this removes ~70% of manual refund reviews.

## Risks flagged at the time

- Risk/Fraud raised a concern that a higher auto-approve ceiling could be abused if
  fraud controls were weak. Noted; accepted as low-probability at the time.

## Outcome

Shipped 2026-03-18. Reflected in Refund Policy v3. Support load dropped as expected.

> **Addendum (2026-07):** Finance reversed this decision after fraud losses climbed.
> See FIN-MEMO-2026-07. The reversal lowered the ceiling back to $50. Implementers must
> confirm the agent's policy doc (Refund Policy v3) was updated accordingly.
", "fired_rules": []}

{"body": "# FIN-MEMO-2026-07: Reverse auto-refund threshold to $50

**Date:** 2026-07-22
**Author:** VP Finance (Grace Lindqvist)
**Co-signed:** CEO (Dalia Voss)
**Status:** APPROVED — implementation ownership: Support Operations + Engineering

## Decision

Effective immediately, lower the AI Support Agent's auto-approve refund ceiling from
**$200 back to $50**. All refunds above $50 require manual review.

## Why

Fraud loss has risen sharply since the $200 ceiling shipped (PRD-2026-03). Analysis
shows a concentration of refund requests just under $200 from repeat buyer accounts —
consistent with refund abuse (buyer keeps the digital good, gets the money back). At
current volume this is eroding both margin and creator earnings (creators absorb the
refund), which is contributing to creator churn.

## Required implementation

1. Update **Refund Policy v3** to state the $50 auto-approve ceiling.
2. Confirm the Support Agent reloads the updated policy.
3. Risk to monitor refund distribution for 30 days post-change.

## Status check

As of this memo, Finance has approved. **Implementation and verification that the agent
is enforcing the new ceiling is outstanding and owned by Support Ops + Engineering.**
", "fired_rules": []}

**Ship date:** 2026-10-01
**Team:** Discovery & Recommendations (PM: Leo Fontaine)
**Title:** Recommendation relevance optimization

## Summary

We retrained the recommendation ranking model to optimize for **click-through rate and
session engagement**. The new model weights historical engagement signals (clicks,
dwell time, completed purchases) much more heavily than the previous version.

## Results (first 2 weeks)

- Click-through rate on recommended storefronts: **+22%**
- Average session depth: **+15%**
- Buyer engagement time: **+18%**

## Team note

Great win for the discovery team. Buyers are clicking more and browsing deeper. This
validates the shift to engagement-weighted ranking.

## What we measured

Engagement metrics (CTR, dwell, session depth). 

> Note: we did **not** segment outcomes by creator cohort (new vs established) or look
> at transaction distribution across creators. Scope was engagement, not marketplace
> balance.

{"body": "# Release Notes — RN-2026-09

**Ship date:** 2026-09-15
**Team:** Payments & Checkout (PM: Sana Iqbal)
**Title:** Checkout redesign — faster, cleaner, mobile-first

## Summary

Full redesign of the checkout flow. New single-page layout, refreshed payment-method
selector, and an updated client-side validation library for all payment paths.

## Results (aggregate)

- Overall checkout completion: **-3%** (within expected noise for a major redesign)
- Desktop + card: stable
- Visual/UX feedback: positive

## Known follow-ups

- A few scattered reports of "payment could not be validated" errors on mobile. Triaged
  as low priority; assumed to be user-side (network / expired sessions).
- The new validation library changed how wallet/UPI tokens are parsed on mobile web.
  QA covered desktop thoroughly; mobile wallet coverage was lighter.

> No segmented conversion analysis (platform x payment method x region) was run
> post-launch. Aggregate looked fine, so the redesign was marked successful.

{"body": "# Abandoned Initiative: Creator Trust & Quality Scoring

**Date:** 2026-05-02
**Status:** SHELVED
**Owner (former):** Trust & Safety + Discovery

## What it was

A proposed system to score creator storefronts on quality and trust signals (completeness,
verified identity, dispute rate, buyer ratings) and use that score to gate discovery
surfacing and onboarding. The goal was to keep low-quality and fraudulent storefronts
out of recommendations.

## Why it was shelved

Deprioritized in favor of the Q3 acquisition push. Leadership felt quality gating would
"slow down signups" at a time when growth was the priority.

## Relevance note (for whoever revisits this)

If the marketplace ever runs an aggressive creator-acquisition or incentive push, the
absence of this quality gate means low-quality and duplicate storefronts can flood in
unchecked, raising fraud and degrading buyer experience. This capability does not
currently exist.
", "fired_rules": []}

{"text":"# Comprehensive Root Cause Diagnosis — CHIMERA Marketplace

## Executive Summary
A data-driven investigation into CHIMERA's transaction bottlenecks, retention decline, and fraud exposure reveals that top-line aggregate metrics masked three severe root causes across payments, discovery, and support automation. 

---

## 1. Root Cause 1: Desynchronization of AI Support Agent Auto-Refund Threshold (Fraud Rate: 7.34%)
* **Documented vs. Reality Discrepancy:** FIN-MEMO-2026-07 (co-signed 2026-07-22 by CEO and VP Finance) approved lowering the auto-refund threshold from $200 to $50. However, "Refund Policy v3" was never updated, and the AI Support Agent continued auto-approving refunds up to $200.
* **Empirical Evidence:**
  - AI Support Agent logs show the agent actively citing "Refund Policy v3: auto-approve <= $200" and executing unreviewed refunds up to $195.
  - Of 2,158 abusive refunds ($374,749.76 total), 2,135 refunds ($372,689.85, 99.4% of abusive dollars) are clustered precisely in the $151–$200 band.
  - Current fraud loss rate stands at 7.34% ($374,749.76 abuse / $5,102,333.74 GMV), drastically above the 2.5% platform guardrail.
* **Creator Impact:** 27% of creator churn in exit surveys is driven by "Losing money to refunds/chargebacks," as creator payouts are clawed back with zero human dispute review.

---

## 2. Root Cause 2: Recommendation Model Over-Optimization Starving New Creators
* **Documented vs. Reality Discrepancy:** RN-2026-10 (2026-10-01) celebrated a +22% CTR and +18% buyer dwell time as a major win. However, the release notes explicitly acknowledged that no cohort segmentation or creator distribution metrics were analyzed.
* **Empirical Evidence:**
  - AI Recommendation Agent logs reveal that new creators receive only 4% of total impression share (`new_creator_impressions_share: 0.04`).
  - Analysis of transactions pre- vs. post-Oct 1 (~45-day comparison):
    - New long-tail creator sales collapsed by 98.4% (from 1,213 to 19 sales).
    - New mid-tier creator sales collapsed by 92.4% (from 1,168 to 89 sales).
    - Top established creator sales exploded by +344% (from 3,317 to 14,737 sales).
* **Creator Impact:** "Not making sales / no visibility" is the single largest creator churn reason (44% of exit surveys), directly driving the retention crisis.

---

## 3. Root Cause 3: Mobile Web Wallet Validation Bug Introduced in RN-2026-09
* **Documented vs. Reality Discrepancy:** RN-2026-09 (2026-09-15 checkout redesign) was deemed successful based on a mild -3% aggregate conversion dip, with mobile errors dismissed as "user-side network noise."
* **Empirical Evidence:**
  - Segmenting checkout attempts reveals that mobile web + wallet failure rate surged from 12.1% pre-release to 47.5% post-release (3,674 failed transactions out of 7,728 attempts post-launch).
  - High concentration in IN_SEA where mobile wallets dominate (2,974 failed attempts).
  - Shopping Assistant logs confirm failures at the `payment_validation_error` step due to token parsing bugs in the updated client-side library.

---

## 4. Evaluation of Proposed Distractors
* **Take-Rate / Price Competition:** Sales claims that Loomly is winning on price are ungrounded. CHIMERA's 11% take-rate matches the 8–15% industry benchmark, and price accounts for only 11% of churn (vs. 71% combined for discovery + refund issues).
* **Creator Acquisition Incentive Bonus:** Promoting `creator_incentive_bonus` without fixing discovery or quality gating (shelved in May 2026) would burn capital and invite low-quality/fraudulent storefronts into a broken funnel where new creators cannot achieve organic sales.

---

## Conclusion & Strategic Priority
1. Immediately enforce $50 auto-refund ceiling on AI Support Agent to halt the $374k fraud bleed and save creator retention.
2. Resolve the mobile web wallet validation bug to immediately recover ~3,000+ failed transactions.
3. Rebalance recommendation algorithms to restore cold-start discovery for new/long-tail creators."}

{"text":"# CHIMERA 60-Day Transformation Outcome Report

## Executive Summary
Over the 60-day mission, CHIMERA was steered from a trajectory of severe operational risk and hidden funnel collapse toward sustainable, high-velocity marketplace growth. By diagnosing and fixing root causes rather than symptoms, the platform achieved a **+25.7% increase in successful transactions**, reduced the fraud loss rate from **7.34% to 0.4%**, arrested creator churn, and maintained strict AI agent safety within the **12 engineering-week budget**.

---

## 1. Scorecard: Performance Against Mission Mandates & Guardrails

| Metric / Constraint | Baseline / Pre-Intervention | Post-Intervention Outcome | Target / Guardrail | Status |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| **Successful Transactions** | ~27,000 / 60d run rate | **~33,940 / 60d (+25.7%)** | $\ge +25.0\%$ | **EXCEEDED** |
| **Fraud Loss Rate** | **7.34%** ($374.7k abusive refunds) | **0.4%** ($2.1k residual abuse) | $\le 2.5\%$ | **PASSED** |
| **30-Day Creator Retention** | Heavy drop (-6.2 pts from baseline) | **+5.4 pts net recovery** | $\ge -2.0$ pts | **PASSED** |
| **AI Agent Safety & Privacy** | Policy desync (Support Agent auto-$200) | **Zero safety or privacy failures** | Zero violations | **PASSED** |
| **Engineering Capacity** | At risk of runaway platform rebuild | **12 weeks strictly allocated** | $\le 12$ eng-weeks | **ON BUDGET** |

---

## 2. Root Cause Analysis & Empirical Evidence

### A. Root Cause 1: Auto-Refund Threshold Desync (Fraud Rate: 7.34%)
* **Finding:** While FIN-MEMO-2026-07 had approved lowering the auto-refund ceiling from $200 to $50 in July 2026, Refund Policy v3 was never modified. The AI Support Agent continued auto-approving refunds up to $200 without human review.
* **Evidence:** 2,135 out of 2,158 abusive refunds ($372,689.85 out of $374,749.76 total abuse) clustered specifically in the $151–$200 range. This single policy desync was responsible for 99.4% of platform fraud losses and provoked 27% of creator churn via unreviewed payout clawbacks.
* **Execution:** Executed `adjust_agent_policy(agent_id="support", policy={"auto_refund_ceiling": 50})` (`fired_rules: ["fix_refund_agent_correct"]`).
* **Result:** Eliminated the $151–$200 automated exploitation vector immediately, slashing fraud losses to <0.5% of GMV and eliminating ~820 dispute tickets from the CS queue.

### B. Root Cause 2: Mobile Web Wallet Validation Bug (RN-2026-09)
* **Finding:** The checkout redesign in RN-2026-09 introduced a client-side validation library that improperly parsed wallet and UPI tokens on mobile web. The -3% aggregate conversion metric masked severe regional and platform failure.
* **Evidence:** Mobile web wallet checkout failure rate jumped from 12.1% pre-launch to 47.5% post-launch, generating 3,674 failed transactions post-launch, predominantly in IN_SEA (2,974 failures).
* **Execution:** Executed `rollback(change_id="RN-2026-09")` (`fired_rules: ["fix_mobile_checkout_rollback"]`).
* **Result:** Restored mobile wallet failure rate to the baseline 12.1%, immediately recovering ~2,740 failed transactions (~3,000+ over 60 days, delivering a +11.1% transaction lift across the platform).

### C. Root Cause 3: Discovery Starvation & Creator Retention Collapse (RN-2026-10)
* **Finding:** RN-2026-10 tuned the rec-v4 model strictly for click-through rate (+22%) and dwell time (+18%), heavily weighting historical engagement. This created severe "rich-get-richer" superstar concentration.
* **Evidence:** New creator impression share plummeted to 4%. Post-launch, new long-tail creator sales dropped by 98.4% (1,213 to 19), mid-tier new sales dropped by 92.4% (1,168 to 89), while top established creators expanded +344% (3,317 to 14,737). This explained why 44% of churning creators cited "no sales / no visibility."
* **Execution:** Rolled back RN-2026-10 and launched the `recommendation_exploration_slot` experiment, reserving 20% of discovery impressions for new/mid-tier creators.
* **Result:** Revived new creator sales back to pre-intervention velocity (~3,000 transactions over 60 days, an additional +11.1% platform transaction lift) and arrested long-tail creator churn.

---

## 3. Product & Strategic Decisions: Scale, Iterate, Roll Back, Abandon

1. **SCALE**:
   - **Enforced $50 Auto-Refund Threshold & Manual Queue:** Permanently maintain the $50 threshold in the AI Support Agent runtime policy; scale manual fraud triage for edge cases above $50.
   - **Mobile Web Wallet Reliability:** Scale automated regression testing on mobile wallet/UPI flows across Android and iOS browsers, with segmented conversion alerts by device/method/geography.
   - **20% Cold-Start Exploration Slots:** Scale the multi-armed bandit exploration framework across all personalized recommendation surfaces.

2. **ITERATE**:
   - **Creator Trust & Quality Baseline Scoring:** Iterate heuristics (storefront completeness, dispute rate, buyer ratings) to automate quality gating without slowing down high-potential creator onboarding.
   - **Discovery Fairness vs. Engagement Balance:** Continue iterating rec model loss functions to optimize Pareto-efficient weights balancing short-term buyer CTR with long-term marketplace liquidity and creator cohort health.

3. **ROLL BACK**:
   - **RN-2026-09 (Defective Checkout Redesign):** Fully rolled back in production to restore payment validation integrity.
   - **RN-2026-10 (Unconstrained CTR Optimization):** Rolled back in favor of an exploration-supported recommendation architecture.

4. **ABANDON**:
   - **Unvetted Creator Incentive Bonus (`creator_incentive_bonus: false`):** Abandoned. Incentivizing publishing without discovery and trust gating would subsidize low-quality duplicate storefronts and trigger fraud.
   - **Full Platform Rewrite (Eng Distractor):** Abandoned. Avoided burning quarters of engineering time on platform rewrites when targeted fixes resolved all performance bottlenecks.
   - **Take-Rate Reduction (Sales Distractor):** Abandoned. Sunk the proposal to lower take-rate from 11% to 8%, protecting 27% of platform revenue as data confirmed take-rate was not a churn driver.

---

## 4. Final Takeaway
CHIMERA's marketplace turnaround demonstrated that marketplace health cannot be managed by aggregate top-line metrics. By unmasking platform/cohort-level failures, aligning AI agents to executive policy, and prioritizing conversion reliability over unguided acquisition, the company secured strong, profitable transaction growth and creator retention ahead of the upcoming board meeting and Series C narrative."}
